Reading and drawing relationships

Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Reading and drawing relationships

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Read relationship limits in both directions. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

2. One borrower, several events

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

Yes. The two directions have different counts. One borrower can have many Loan rows. Each Loan row has one required borrower reference. Ask students to state the direction before naming the relationship. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

3. Minimum and maximum participation

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with teacher explanation

Zero means optional participation. Exactly one means minimum one and maximum one. The Equipment–Loan rule follows the same pattern: an item can have zero or many loans over time, and each loan has exactly one item. Read the symbols at one end as the number there for one instance at the other end. Rules come from requirements, not only the observed sample. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

4. The four-table equipment model

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher modelling

Two bars mark exactly one. A circle and a crow’s foot mark zero or many. Read Category–Equipment, Borrower–Loan and Equipment–Loan in both directions. Each parent permits zero or many children; each child requires exactly one parent. PK means primary key and FK means foreign key. Primary keys are underlined. Original diagram source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/equipment-model.svg . Notation reference: SCSA support booklet, printed page 15 (PDF page 19). The diagram’s placements can change without changing its meaning. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

5. Three relationship patterns

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

The locker example states maximum participation only. Whether a borrower must have a locker is a separate minimum-participation rule. Borrowing across time is many to many between Borrower and Equipment; Loan resolves it into two one-to-many relationships and stores event facts. This does not permit two active loans for the same physical item simultaneously. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

6. An independent four-table diagram

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 4, 5 and 8. Hide the worked model while learners draw, then compare. Category–Equipment, Equipment–Loan and Borrower–Loan all have optional-many at the child end and exactly-one at the parent end. Preserve all four tables and their fields. Ask partners to explain how the required FK is on the many side. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

7. A category with no items

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

C04 is allowed because a category may have zero items. An Equipment row with no CategoryID breaks the required category rule. Students should point to the appropriate end of the relationship instead of assuming all participation is mandatory. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

8. History and current availability

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

History records events over time. The minimum/maximum relationship does not by itself enforce the separate no-overlap rule for active loans. The application or database needs an appropriate additional check. Ask for one unreturned and one returned example rather than assuming every Loan row is current. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.
